enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an example of computer simulation?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A simulation uses a computer model to imitate a real situation so that it can be studied safely and cheaply.

### Solution

A flight simulator imitates the behaviour of a real aircraft, so trainee pilots can practise without any risk. Writing a letter, printing and copying files are ordinary data processing, not the imitation of a real system. **Answer: a.**

choix.texte: A flight simulator used to train pilots
A word processor used to write a letter
A program that copies files to a flash drive

enonce_markdown: State **two** advantages of using a computer simulation to test the design of a bridge instead of building a real bridge first.  *[2 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare a simulation with a real experiment in terms of cost, time, safety and the possibility to repeat the test.

### Solution

Any two of the following:

- It is much cheaper, because no materials are used.
- It is safer, because nobody is in danger if the design fails.
- It is faster, and the test can be repeated many times with different values (load, wind, length).
- A dangerous or extreme situation can be tested which could not be produced in real life.

enonce_markdown: A manager changes the value in one input cell of a spreadsheet model, and all the results update automatically. Which feature of the model makes this possible?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A model links its results to its inputs. In a spreadsheet, this link is made with formulas that refer to the input cells.

### Solution

The result cells contain formulas that refer to the input cell, so a change in the input is recalculated everywhere. Currency format, charts and sorting only change the appearance or the order of data. **Answer: c.**

choix.texte: The cells are formatted as currency.
The rows are sorted in alphabetical order.
The results are calculated by formulas that refer to the input cell.
A chart has been drawn next to the table.

enonce_markdown: Which of the following situations is **best** studied with a computer simulation rather than a real experiment?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Simulation is most useful when a real test would be dangerous, very expensive, very slow or impossible to repeat.

### Solution

Testing how a building behaves in a strong earthquake in real life would be destructive and dangerous, so it is modelled on a computer. Checking spelling, calculating a payroll and copying files are simple processing tasks, with no need to imitate a real system. **Answer: b.**

choix.texte: Checking the spelling of a letter
Predicting how a building will behave in a strong earthquake
Calculating the monthly salary of workers
Copying a folder to another drive

enonce_markdown:
A trader models his weekly profit with the formulas

units sold = 1000 - 1.5 × price

profit = (price - 350) × units sold

(price in FCFA, cost per unit 350 FCFA). He tests the prices 450, 500 and 600 FCFA. Which price does the model predict will give the greatest profit?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Run the model for each value of the input, calculate the profit each time, then compare the outputs. This is what-if analysis.

### Solution

- Price 450: units = 1000 - 675 = 325; profit = 100 × 325 = 32 500 FCFA.
- Price 500: units = 1000 - 750 = 250; profit = 150 × 250 = 37 500 FCFA.
- Price 600: units = 1000 - 900 = 100; profit = 250 × 100 = 25 000 FCFA.

The greatest profit is for a price of **500 FCFA**. **Answer: c.**

choix.texte: 450 FCFA (the lowest price sells the most)
The three prices give the same profit

enonce_markdown: A computer model of the traffic at a busy junction in Douala predicts that cars never wait more than 10 seconds, but in real life long queues form. State **two** possible reasons why the model is inaccurate and **one** way to improve it.  *[3 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A model is a simplified version of reality. Its results are only as good as its assumptions and the data used to build it.

### Solution

Possible reasons (any two):

- The model ignores real factors such as pedestrians, motorbike taxis, rain, accidents or traffic lights failing.
- The data used (number of cars per hour) is old or was collected at the wrong times of the day.
- The assumptions are wrong, for example that every driver obeys the rules.

Improvement (any one): collect real traffic counts at different times, add the missing factors to the model, then compare its predictions with real observations and adjust the model until they agree.
